column1: # Game profile of Toy Story 3 Complete Edition (Switch, update v196608 = 1.0.3). Plays on a Galaxy S23 Ultra (Android 17, Adreno 740):
# the publisher logos, the opening movie, the first level (Woody's Roundup town, Bullseye, Hamm), a mission, the game's save and the
# pause menu, at 30 fps as on the Switch.
# Digital Eclipse's Octane engine on NVN, SDK 21.4.4, restored from Avalanche's 2010 source: modules main + sdk; FMOD (its own AudioOut)
# beside the SDK's audio renderer, Bink movies. The RomFS keeps its assets in 1,903 Octane zips (end-of-central-directory record first,
# CRCs zero), and the 3,070 NVN shaders are in the .tfx effects of assets/effects/fx_new.zip beside the PC build's D3D9 bytecode
# (shader_split.py octane_members / octane_shaders). The skinned characters fetch their bone indices as R8G8B8A8_USCALED (D3D9 UBYTE4),
# which the Adreno 740 cannot fetch: with DM_VK_SCALED_FETCH=1 (android.tsv) the host fetches them as UINT and converts in the vertex shader.
# Memory: the survey's values, unchanged (main sets a heap; no system resource).
# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the Android app's name is this one unless --app-name is given
# main sets a heap of at most the pool − 64 MB: a 3328 MB heap region
# the NPDM declares 0 MB of system resource: IsVirtualAddressMemoryEnabled is false, as on Horizon (Big Brain Academy: Brain vs. Brain sets a heap only then)
# Octane zips: the 3,070 NVN shaders are in the .tfx effects of assets/effects/fx_new.zip (shader_split.py octane_shaders)
